extracted.intended_audience: university technology transfer offices, small business and nonprofit contractors, and federal contracting/agency officials
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and procedural standards (37 C.F.R. Part 401) governing ownership, reporting, clause use, appeals, march-in, and related duties for subject inventions arising under federal funding agreements with small businesses and nonprofit organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope / subject invention coverage (§401.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions conceived or first actually reduced to practice in performance of a government-funded project are subject to these regulations; separate non-government-sponsored projects that fall outside planned/committed activities are not subject. Separate accounting is not determinative; time relationship or use of fundamental knowledge between projects is not determinative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (1) Industry-sponsored project that applies new knowledge generated by a government project may be outside scope if it falls outside the planned/committed activities. (2) An instrument purchased with government funds later used (without interference or cost to the government-funded project) to make an invention funded entirely by non-government funds is not a subject invention. Challenges to contractor assertions that an invention is not a subject invention are appealable under §401.11(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability and precedence (§401.1(b),(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: This part implements 35 U.S.C. 202–204 and applies to all Federal agencies and to funding agreements with small business firms and nonprofit organizations executed after the part's effective date, except funding agreements made primarily for educational purposes. The regulation supersedes OMB Circular A-124 and takes precedence over inconsistent agency regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: March-in and appeals procedures (§§401.6 and 401.11) apply to proceedings initiated after the effective date even if the funding agreement predated the part. Agencies must conform their regulations to this part; only contractor-requested deviations not inconsistent with Chapter 18 may be made without Secretary approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (key terms) (§401.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authoritative definitions used throughout the part, including: funding agreement; contractor; invention; subject invention; practical application; made; small business firm; nonprofit organization; Chapter 18; Secretary; electronically filed; electronic or optical-electronic system; patent application; initial patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select definitions of particular practical importance: • 'funding agreement' = any contract, grant, or cooperative agreement between a Federal agency and a contractor for experimental, developmental, or research work (includes assignments, substitutions, subcontracts). • 'subject invention' = any invention of a contractor conceived or first actually reduced to practice in performance of work under a funding agreement. • 'practical application' = manufacture (product), practice (process/method), or operate (machine/system) under conditions that establish utilization and availability to the public on reasonable terms. • 'made' = conception or first actual reduction to practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the standard patent rights clause (§401.3 / §401.14 requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each funding agreement awarded to a small business firm or nonprofit organization (except those subject to 35 U.S.C. 212) shall contain the clause found in §401.14(a) with authorized modifications/tailoring. Alternative provisions may be included in specified circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorized alternatives include: contractor not located in U.S.; exceptional circumstances where restriction of retention of title better promotes policy objectives; foreign intelligence/counterintelligence; DOE naval nuclear propulsion/weapons-related programs. When alternate paragraph (b) is appropriate (e.g., CRADA work), contracting officers must ensure appeal procedures of §401.4 are satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency exceptions — written determination and justification (§401.3(e),(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Before using exceptions to the standard clause, the agency must prepare a written determination including a statement of facts supporting the determination and, where §401.3(a)(2) is used, an analysis justifying how the alternate provisions better achieve the objectives of 35 U.S.C. 200.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A separate statement of facts is required for each exceptional-circumstances determination (a single determination may apply in appropriate cases to related agreements/subcontracts). The contractor/prospective contractor must be promptly provided with the determination, facts, analysis (if any), and notification of appeal rights under 35 U.S.C. 202(b)(4) and §401.4. Except for national security determinations under §401.3(a)(3), copies must be provided to the Secretary within 30 days after award; copies to SBA Chief Counsel for Advocacy when the agreement is with a small business. Secretary may recommend corrective actions if determinations are contrary to policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualification/certification for the standard clause (§401.3(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for the standard clause, a prospective contractor may be required to certify that it is a small business firm or a nonprofit organization. The agency may require evidence of nonprofit status or file a protest concerning small business status (13 CFR 121.9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should verify status when reason to question exists; qualification affects entitlement to the standard patent rights clause and related rights under the part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor appeals of exception determinations (§401.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: A contractor has the right to administrative review of a determination to use an exception (§401.3(a)(1)–(4)) if it believes the determination is contrary to chapter policies or an abuse of discretion. The appeal procedure and timelines are specified in §401.4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key procedures/timelines: • Contractor must give written notice within 30 working days of receiving the determination (or longer if agency regulation permits). • Appeal decided by agency head or designee above originator. • If genuine dispute over material facts, fact-finding is to be undertaken (informal as practicable; opportunities to appear with counsel, submit evidence, witnesses; transcribed record available at cost unless waived). • Fact-finding should be completed within 45 working days of agency receipt of written notice. • Agency decision based on facts found and arguments; after fact-finding the decision due within 30 working days, or within 45 working days if no fact-finding. • Contractor may petition U.S. Claims Court within 60 days after determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modification and tailoring of standard clauses (§401.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may complete blanks and replace italicized words in §401.14 clauses to suit the particular funding agreement (e.g., 'contract' → 'grant', 'contractor' → 'grantee'). Grants/cooperative agreements may delete certain paragraphs to apply clause to subcontractors. Agencies should designate a central communications point in paragraph (l).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible additional modifications include: (a) adding language to permit government sublicensing of foreign governments/international organizations under specified treaties or agreements; (b) unilateral amendment language for long-term performance identifying new treaties; (c) adding subparagraphs to require contractor reports before close-out, provide patent filing data upon request, or provide periodic listings of disclosed subject inventions; (d) facility-specific revenue use and royalty-sharing rules for nonprofit operators of government-owned facilities; (e) requiring contractors for government-owned facilities to establish and submit procedures to ensure prompt identification and timely disclosure of subject inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency reporting and recordkeeping obligations (§401.3(g), §401.5(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must accumulate and, upon request of the Comptroller General, provide totals of prime agreements containing the patent rights clause for each fiscal year beginning Oct 1, 1982. Agencies must also provide copies of exception determinations and supporting facts/analysis to the Secretary (and SBA Chief Counsel where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of determinations must be sent within 30 days after award. These reporting obligations assist oversight and conformity with Chapter 18 policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-finding procedural standards in appeals and march-in proceedings (§401.4(b)(3); §401.6(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Fact-finding shall be as informal as practicable and consistent with fundamental fairness, affording contractor opportunity to appear with counsel, submit documentary evidence, present witnesses, and confront agency witnesses. A transcribed record shall be made and available at cost unless waived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When fact-finding is used, the official must prepare written findings of fact and recommended decision, and transmit them to the agency head or designee. The agency head may reject only those facts clearly erroneous and must state basis for contrary finding. Timeframes for fact-finding and subsequent decisions are specified in the appeals and march-in sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: March-in rights exercise procedures (§401.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures govern exercise of march-in rights under 35 U.S.C. 203: agency notification to contractor when it receives information that might warrant march-in, opportunity for informal comment (30 days), initiation of formal march-in proceeding with written notice specifying reasons and fields of use, and opportunity to present opposition and evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key procedural points: • If contractor submits comments, agency must either initiate formal procedures within 60 days of receiving the comment or notify contractor it will not pursue march-in. • Upon initiation, contractor/assignee/exclusive licensee has 30 days to submit opposition or raise genuine disputes of material facts; fact-finding triggered if disputes arise. • Fact-finding procedures parallel appeals (informal fairness, counsel, transcribed record). • Any portion of proceeding relating to utilization or efforts to obtain utilization is closed to the public and such information is not disclosed outside government except with contractor authorization. • Official must prepare findings and recommended determination, provide parties 30 days to submit written arguments, and, upon request, hold oral arguments before the agency head. Determination must be based on facts found and consideration of consistency with 35 U.S.C. 200 policy/objectives.
